core_summary: Light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation of light). Materials are transparent (allow light fully), translucent (allow light partially), or opaque (block light completely). Shadows are dark regions formed on a screen when opaque objects obstruct light paths. Pinhole cameras demonstrate rectilinear propagation by forming real, inverted images. Reflection of light occurs when light hits smooth polished surfaces (plane mirrors), following the Law of Reflection: Angle of Incidence equals Angle of Reflection (i = r). Plane mirror images are virtual, erect, same size as object, and laterally inverted.
key_concepts: To construct a card pinhole camera and observe real inverted image formation.

key_terms.definition: 1. Angle of Incidence (i) = Angle of Reflection (r). 2. Incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in the same plane.
The reversal of left and right orientation in an image formed by a plane mirror.

key_takeaways: Angle of incidence is ALWAYS measured between the incident light ray and the normal (perpendicular 90-degree line).
